eta.notes: All visitors to Kenya who are not exempt must apply for an eTA online before travel at https://etakenya.go.ke - Kenya abolished visas entirely in January 2024, so the eTA is the entry authorisation itself, not a layer on top of a visa. Exempt: EAC citizens and (since 2025) most African nationalities, which appear as visa-free entries; Somalia and Libya are excluded from the African exemption and still require an eTA. Types and fees: Transit eTA $20; Standard eTA (single entry, up to 90 days) $30; One Year Multi-Entry eTA $300; Five Year Multi-Entry eTA $185 (US nationals only). Processing time capped at 72 hours (expedited option introduced 2025).

visa_policy.notes: Kenya replaced its traditional visa system with an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) system operated by the Ministry of Interior and National Administration (immigration.go.ke / evisa.go.ke). Legal Notice No. 93 (issued 30 May 2025) introduced the Seventeenth Schedule via the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025, establishing the full eTA exemption list. The exemption covers: EAC Partner States (180 days), 45 non-African nations including Pacific/Caribbean/Commonwealth/ASEAN states (90 days), and 28 additional African nations (60 days). Somalia and Libya are explicitly excluded from the African bloc due to security concerns and require eTA. There is no longer a visa-on-arrival or separate e-visa category.

visa_types.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA)
visa_types.notes: Required for all foreign nationals (replacing visa-on-arrival and prior visa systems effective January 2024). Applied online at etakenya.go.ke. USD 30 fee. Approved eTA allows 90-day stay, extendable. Holders of East African Community (EAC) passports and some nationalities may be exempt. Not the same as visa-free entry - eTA is mandatory pre-travel authorization for most nationalities.

visa_types.name: Transit Electronic Travel Authorisation (Transit eTA)
visa_types.purpose: Travellers connecting through Kenya to a third country, for a stay of up to 72 hours
visa_types.notes: Transit category of Kenya's eTA for passengers transiting through a Kenyan airport en route to another country, for a total stay not exceeding 72 hours. Official fee USD 20. Applied online before travel at etakenya.go.ke; processing capped at 72 hours. eTA-exempt nationals do not require it.

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class D (Employment)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign employees offered specific employment by a specific employer for skills not available in Kenya
visa_types.notes: Kenya's main employer-sponsored work permit. Issued to a person offered specific employment by a specific employer, who holds skills or qualifications not available in Kenya and whose engagement benefits the country. Requires employer sponsorship. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 500,000 per year (~USD 3,850); gratis for East African Community citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class C (Prescribed Profession)
visa_types.purpose: Members of a prescribed profession (e.g. medicine, law, engineering) intending to practise it in Kenya
visa_types.notes: Issued to a member of a prescribed profession who intends to practise that profession, alone or in partnership, in Kenya and whose practice benefits the country. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class G (Specific Trade, Business or Consultancy)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals establishing or running a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession in Kenya (self-employment/investor)
visa_types.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession (other than a prescribed profession) in Kenya. Requires documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital to invest. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke). Corrected 2026-07: the prior entry mis-stated the fee (USD 2,000) and described employer-sponsored employment, which is actually Class D.

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class B (Agriculture and Animal Husbandry)
visa_types.purpose: Investors engaging in agriculture or animal husbandry in Kenya
visa_types.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in agriculture or animal husbandry in Kenya, with suitable land and sufficient capital. Requires documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class F (Specific Manufacturing)
visa_types.purpose: Investors engaging in a specific manufacturing activity in Kenya
visa_types.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in a specific manufacture in Kenya. Requires documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital for manufacturing. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class A (Prospecting and Mining)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals engaging, alone or in partnership, in prospecting for minerals or mining in Kenya
visa_types.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in prospecting for minerals or mining in Kenya. Requires the necessary prospecting/mining rights and licences and documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital to invest. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 500,000 per year (~USD 3,850); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke). Added 2026-07 to complete the work-permit class enumeration; the Class A investor route already appears in this record's rbi section.

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class I (Approved Religious and Charitable Activities)
visa_types.purpose: Missionaries and staff of approved religious or charitable (non-profit) organisations
visa_types.notes: Issued to a member of a society registered under the Societies Act engaged as a missionary, or with a government-approved non-profit organisation, whose presence benefits Kenya. Official fees: processing KES 5,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 50,000 per year (~USD 385); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class K (Ordinary Residents)
visa_types.purpose: Financially independent residents aged 35+ living on assured non-employment income (pension/annuity) - Kenya's retirement/passive-income residence permit
visa_types.notes: Kenya's closest equivalent to a retirement permit. Issued to a person at least 35 years old with an assured annual income of not less than USD 24,000 from sources outside Kenya (e.g. pension or annuity), not derived from employment or business in Kenya; the holder may not take employment. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Class N Digital Nomad Work Permit
visa_types.purpose: Remote workers and freelancers earning income from companies or clients registered outside Kenya
visa_types.notes: Introduced October 2024; online applications opened April 2025. Issued to a person who works remotely within Kenya for a company registered outside the country, or who provides self-employed services to overseas clients. Validity one or two years, renewable. The holder may not be employed by a Kenyan company or earn income within Kenya. Official fees: processing USD 200 (non-refundable) plus issuance USD 1,000 per year. Requires the last three months' bank statements or payslips as proof of income. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Special Pass
visa_types.purpose: Short-term (up to 6 months) work, trade or professional engagement, often as a bridge while a work permit is processed
visa_types.notes: Authorisation to enter and remain in Kenya for a period not exceeding 6 months to temporarily conduct business, trade or a profession (e.g. equipment installation, training, short consultancy), or as a bridge while a work-permit application is pending. Official fee USD 200 per month for non-EAC nationals; gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Student's Pass
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals accepted or admitted to study at a Kenyan academic or training institution
visa_types.notes: Issued to a foreigner accepted or admitted to a recognised Kenyan academic or training institution. Official fee USD 100 per year for non-EAC nationals; gratis for East African Community citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke). Minors require parental consent; refugees require Department of Refugee Services clearance. Fee corrected from prior USD 50 to the official USD 100/year on 2026-07 re-validation; official_url updated from the retired eCitizen link.

visa_types.name: Internship/Research Pass
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals undertaking an internship or academic research in Kenya
visa_types.notes: Authorisation to enter and remain in Kenya to undertake an internship or academic research. Researchers require NACOSTI clearance and institutional sponsorship. Official fee KES 15,000 per year (~USD 115) for non-EAC nationals; gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Dependant's Pass
visa_types.purpose: Spouses, children and other dependants of Kenyan citizens, permit holders, permanent residents or exempted persons
visa_types.notes: For a foreigner who is a dependant of a Kenyan citizen, permit/pass holder, permanent resident or exempted person; validity is typically co-terminus with the sponsor's status. Official fees: KES 20,000 (~USD 155) for a spouse or child of a Kenyan citizen, KES 10,000 (~USD 77) for a spouse or child of a work-permit or permanent-residence holder; gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

visa_types.name: Work Permit Class M (Refugees)
visa_types.purpose: Persons granted refugee status in Kenya, and their spouses, wishing to take up a specific occupation, trade, business or profession
visa_types.notes: Issued to a person who has been granted refugee status in Kenya, and their spouse, wishing to engage in a specific occupation, trade, business or profession. Issued gratis (free of charge). Requires refugee status recognition; applied via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

cbi.notes: No citizenship-by-investment program found on any official Kenyan government source. The immigration.go.ke website lists citizenship acquisition routes: by birth, descent, registration (including by marriage after 7 years), and naturalization. No investment route to citizenship is listed or offered officially.

programs.name: Class G Permit - Specific Trade, Business or Consultancy
programs.notes: Issued to a person who intends to engage, alone or in partnership, in a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession in Kenya. Requires documentary proof of capital to be invested of at least USD 100,000. Processing fee: KShs 20,000 (non-refundable); Issuance fee: KShs 250,000 per year. EAC Member States citizens: Gratis. Path to permanent residence or citizenship not stated verbatim on the official page.

programs.name: Class A Permit - Prospecting and Mining
programs.notes: Issued to a person who intends to engage in prospecting for minerals or mining in Kenya. Requires proof of funds for investment of at least USD 100,000, plus necessary prospecting/mining rights and licenses. Processing fee: KShs 20,000 (non-refundable); Issuance fee: KShs 500,000 per year. EAC Member States citizens: Gratis.

programs.name: Class N Permit - Digital Nomad (KEP/N)
programs.eligibility: Foreign nationals who work remotely within Kenya for a company registered outside Kenya: under employment contract, as shareholder or business representative of a foreign company, or self-employed serving clients outside Kenya. Must provide bank statements or payslips for last 3 months proving income.
programs.notes: Permit issued for 1 or 2 years, renewable. Processing fee: USD 200 (non-refundable); Issuance fee: USD 1,000 per year. Applications accepted from April 2025 per official eFNS portal. Apply via https://fns.immigration.go.ke.

validation_notes: 2026-06-29: RE-VALIDATION - No changes. Full re-fetch of evisa.go.ke/general-information confirmed all 6 EAC (180-day), 44 non-African (90-day), and 28 African (60-day) visa_free entries are accurate and match live official page. Searched Kenya Law gazette for any 2026 amendments to eTA exemption list - none found. Legal Notice 121/2025 (2025-07-16) was also fetched and confirmed to be a work-permit fee exemption for specific infrastructure companies, not an eTA nationality exemption change. Record is fully current as of 2026-06-29.

2026-06-27: ADDED Samoa (WSM) to 90-day visa_free list - confirmed present on official evisa.go.ke/general-information page and in EIG Law and CDH analyses of Legal Notice No. 93 Seventeenth Schedule. Was entirely missing from the prior record.

2026-06-27: CORRECTED Seychelles (SYC) from 90-day to 60-day - the official government page evisa.go.ke/general-information explicitly lists Seychelles under the 60-day African bloc. Per safety rules, classified conservatively at 60 days to match the official government website display. Note: EIG Law analysis of the Seventeenth Schedule PDF shows Seychelles appearing in both 90-day and 60-day lists in the legal notice text; the ambiguity in the underlying gazette is noted in gaps.

PREVIOUSLY NOTED (prior run): ADDED Solomon Islands (SLB) to 90-day visa_free list - present in Legal Notice No. 93 Seventeenth Schedule per EIG Law and CDH analyses. Not displayed on evisa.go.ke/general-information page but confirmed in direct legal analyses of the gazette.

PREVIOUSLY NOTED (prior run): UPDATED eta.notes to explicitly state Somalia and Libya are excluded from the African eTA-exemption bloc due to security concerns, and to note the expedited 72-hour processing cap introduced in 2025.
PREVIOUSLY NOTED (prior run): UPDATED visa_policy.source_urls to include the Kenya High Commission (London) PDF copy of Legal Notice No. 93 as an additional official source.
No changes to conditional_access, cbi, rbi, or fast_track sections - all verified against official sources as accurate.

CORRECTED 2026-07-10: the blanket eTA entry was labelled "All nationalities not listed as eTA-exempt", which the dataset builder treats as an unresolvable negation and skips - only 40 enumerated nationalities received eTA edges and every other passport (incl. India, China) fell through to visa-required: a false harder-access error. Relabelled to a plain "All nationalities" catch-all; visa-free (exempt) entries outrank it during resolution, so exempt countries are unaffected.
gaps: Seychelles dual-listing ambiguity: EIG Law analysis of the Seventeenth Schedule PDF shows Seychelles appearing in both the 90-day and the 60-day African bloc in the legal notice text. The official evisa.go.ke website displays Seychelles in the 60-day category only. The raw gazette PDF text cannot be directly parsed. Classified conservatively at 60 days per the official government display. Recommend re-checking once a readable version of the gazette is available.

Solomon Islands (SLB): Confirmed in EIG Law and CDH analyses of LN 93 Seventeenth Schedule as 90-day exempt, but not enumerated on the evisa.go.ke/general-information display page. Retained in record per prior validation.
Maximum stay duration for eTA-required nationalities is not enumerated per nationality on the official evisa.go.ke page - the page only shows eTA-required vs eTA-exempt.
Path to permanent residency or citizenship for Class G and Class A permit holders not stated verbatim on official immigration.go.ke pages.
Class F (specific manufacturing) permit details found in search snippet but not directly scraped from an official page - only Class A and Class G were directly verified.
Dual citizenship allowance for Kenya not confirmed from an official source during this research session.
Five Year Multi-Entry eTA ($185) listed as for 'American nationals' only - maximum stay per entry not explicitly stated on official eligibility page.

No Type A (held third-country credential) conditional rules found: the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025 Seventeenth Schedule contains no exemptions based on holding a US visa, UK visa, Schengen visa, foreign residence permit, Green Card, or OCI card. These categories were specifically searched and not found on any official Kenyan government source.
No OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholder special-status rule for Kenya found on any official Kenyan government domain.

Serving Members of the British Military (item 34 of Seventeenth Schedule) appear in the conditional_access array under special_status basis but the precise qualifying document is not enumerated in the official text - only employment status is referenced.
Seychelles 90-day vs 60-day categorization: the underlying gazette PDF shows both listings per EIG Law; evisa.go.ke shows 60-day. Direct PDF parse not possible.

outbound_official.note: No official Kenya government outbound visa-list page located; rely on destination-side data. Searched mfa.go.ke/kenya-citizens, mfa.go.ke/kenyans-citizens, immigration.go.ke, immigration.ecitizen.go.ke, support.ecitizen.go.ke - none publish an authoritative list of destinations where Kenya ordinary-passport holders may travel without a prior consular visa. The support.ecitizen.go.ke domain hosts informational blog-style articles on this topic but the server returns empty responses or SSL errors to external clients and the pages are not structured as an official registry.
